eyebrow: Azure & AWS Cloud Security Engineering · Chapter 2
titlePlain: Azure RBAC vs. Azure Policy: When Each One Is the
subtitle: Lesson 7 · Azure Identity & Access Security

steps.label: Azure RBAC
steps.sub: can this principal attempt this action at all? Evaluated at authorization time, before anything happens

steps.label: Azure Policy
steps.sub: is this resource's configuration allowed, regardless of who created it?

steps.label: Both can apply to the same resource
steps.sub: RBAC authorizes the attempt; Policy judges the result

code:
{
  "Actions": ["Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write"],
  "NotActions": [],
  "DataActions": ["Microsoft.Storage/.../blobs/read"],
  "NotDataActions": [],
  "AssignableScopes": ["/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<rg>"]
}
# Contributor = Actions "*" minus NotActions for granting access
# DataActions govern the data plane separately from management plane
caption: A custom role is a different combination of Actions/NotActions/DataActions than any built-in.

eyebrow: What a Policy effect actually does
code:
# Deny              -> blocks the non-compliant write entirely
# Audit              -> allows it, flags non-compliant in the dashboard
# AuditIfNotExists   -> flags if a related resource is missing
# DeployIfNotExists  -> actively deploys the missing related resource
# Modify             -> adds/updates/removes properties or tags at write time
caption: An Owner can still be Denied by Policy -- RBAC never evaluated the resource's own configuration.

steps.label: RBAC alone
steps.sub: stops the wrong people from creating storage accounts, misses a mistake by the right people

steps.label: Policy alone
steps.sub: catches the misconfiguration, but anyone could still attempt the creation

steps.label: Together
steps.sub: restrict the action with a custom role, constrain the result with a Deny-effect policy
